To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
rDNA content and rRNA synthesis are differentially regulated in various tissues of adult Drosophila.
the amount of rRNA genes in D. melanogaster is not constant throughout growth and development, and that there is no evidence of a correlation between rDNA redundancy and polyteny.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of rDNA in Drosophilla melanogaster.
the regulation of ribosomal RNA synthesis in Drosophyla melanogaster.
the study of ribosomal RNA genes (rDNA) in Drosophia melanogaster.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in Drosophyla melanogaster, underreplication of ribosomal RNA genes does not necessarily accompany polyteny, and that the amount of ribosomal DNA does not determine the rate of ribosome formation.
the amount of rDNA present in D. melanogaster tissues is regulated at the level of transcription.
the amount of rRNA synthesized is determined by the number of genes and that this number is constant in all tissues except the salivary glands and the ovaries of larvae and pupae, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in Drosophilla, as in other eucaryotes, rRNA genes are underreplicated in certain tissues, and that the extent of this underreplication is dependent on the tissue and on the genotype.
rDNA is not a constant feature in the genome of Drosophilla melanogaster and that the amount of precursor RNA synthesized in various tissues is regulated in accordance with the needs of the organism.
rDNA content and rDNA activity vary independently in Drosophia melanogaster.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amount of rRNA genes present does not necessarily reflect the amount of rDNA activity.
rDNA activity is controlled at several levels, i.e. at the transcriptional level as well as at the level of rDNA redundancy.
the amount of rDNA is not necessarily a good indicator of the level of rRNA synthesis.
